packet.evaluation_question: Explain baseline investigations and how subsequent inflammatory-marker readings should be used.

evidence.text: Measure baseline C-reactive protein concentration when starting antibiotic treatment in babies who may have neonatal infection. Use this together with any subsequent readings to assess the likelihood of infection and response to treatment. [2021]

Take account of blood gentamicin concentrations when deciding on subsequent gentamicin dosing regimen (see the section on therapeutic drug monitoring for babies receiving gentamicin). [2012] 1.20.7 Record the times of: • gentamicin administration • sampling for therapeutic monitoring. [2012]

When interpreting the results of cerebrospinal fluid investigations, take into account: • red cells in the sample, which may suggest blood contamination or a different diagnosis • whether earlier antibiotics may have reduced the diagnostic reliability of these investigations. [2024]

The Kaiser Permanente neonatal sepsis calculator can be used as an alternative to the framework outlined in recommendation 1.10.3 for babies born after 34+0 weeks of pregnancy who are being cared for in a neonatal unit, transitional care or postnatal ward. It should only be used if it is part of a prospective audit, which should record: • total number of babies assessed using the calculator • number of babies correctly identified by the calculator who develop a culture-confirmed neonatal infection • number of babies incorrectly identified by the calculator who do not develop a culture-confirmed neonatal infection • number of babies missed by the calculator who develop a culture-confirmed neonatal infection. [2021]

claims.text: Obtain a baseline C‑reactive protein (CRP) measurement at the time antibiotics are initiated for any infant with suspected early‑onset sepsis.

support.quote: Measure baseline C-reactive protein concentration when starting antibiotic treatment in babies who may have neonatal infection.

claims.text: Repeat CRP at 12‑hour intervals (or as clinically indicated) and interpret trends together with the initial value to gauge infection likelihood and treatment response.

support.quote: Use this together with any subsequent readings to assess the likelihood of infection and response to treatment.

claims.text: A falling CRP trend after baseline supports a decreasing probability of ongoing infection, whereas a rising or persistently high CRP suggests continued risk and may prompt reassessment of antimicrobial therapy.

support.quote: Use this together with any subsequent readings to assess the likelihood of infection and response to treatment.

claims.text: If subsequent CRP values rise or fail to decline within 24‑48 hours, consider escalation to broader‑spectrum antibiotics, additional cultures, or imaging, especially in the context of clinical deterioration.

support.quote: Use this together with any subsequent readings to assess the likelihood of infection and response to treatment.

claims.text: Document the timing of each CRP draw relative to antibiotic start to ensure accurate trend interpretation.

support.quote: Measure baseline C-reactive protein concentration when starting antibiotic treatment in babies who may have neonatal infection.

claims.text: Explain to parents that CRP is an inflammatory marker used to track infection progress; a decreasing result is reassuring, while a rising result may indicate the need for further investigation.
